sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2018. Two birds with one stone: The aerodynamic voicing constraint and the languages of Borneo. JSEALS 11(2): 1-18.
sources.note: Berawan (Long Terawan, Batu Belah, Long Teru, Long Jegan) cited only for nasalization of voiced stop codas (Table 7); the stress statement on p. 5 ('stress is penultimate on all lexical bases...') is about Kelabit, not Berawan.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (revised edition). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Berawan appears for final-consonant reduction (p. 221), intervocalic devoicing, gemination of the onset of open final syllables ('the phonetic motivation behind these conditions, if any, remains puzzling'), and low vowel fronting (pp. 667-671); the stress survey (4.3.2.1 'Stress rules', pp. 251ff) discusses Kelabit, Kiput and Narum ('stress is final') but never Berawan.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. Berawan language (wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Summarises Burkhardt 2014 pp. 197-214 (Proto-Berawan sound changes: antepenult neutralisation, schwa geminating the following consonant, low-vowel fronting); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Burkhardt, Jürgen M. 2025. The Berawan comparative glossary: motivation, challenges and undergirding principles. Journal of Borneo-Kalimantan 11. doi:10.33736/jbk.8818.2025
sources.note: Glossary-design paper; scattered phonological remarks (penult vowel lowering in Long Jegan); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Burkhardt, Jürgen M., Jey Lingam Burkhardt & Lay Hoon Ang. 2020. One orthography, four lects: The unified Berawan orthography. Journal of Borneo-Kalimantan 6(1): 1-21. doi:10.33736/jbk.2411.2020
sources.note: Phonological comparison of all four lects (incl. Batu Belah and Long Teru = zbc), explicitly 'taken from Burkhardt (2014)': consonant and vowel inventories, single vs geminate consonants, automatic gemination after penult schwa, phonemic vowel length in the ultima. Zero occurrences of 'stress' or 'accent'; silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1992. The long consonants of Long Terawan. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 148(3): 409-427. doi:10.1163/22134379-90003144
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Long Terawan Berawan (= West Berawan zbw), not Central. Gives the phoneme inventory (p. 412) and consonant-length contrasts; 'stress' occurs only for Brunei Malay loans ('where SM has penultimate stress, BM generally has final stress', p. 415) and in a footnote quoting Thurgood's cross-linguistic generalisation about geminates (p. 412 n.); no statement of Berawan stress placement.
